slides.title: How to complete this workbook
steps: Every slide with a green DRAFT — CONFIRM OR CORRECT badge was pre-filled from your foundation documents and live LFX data. Edit directly on the slide: strike what is wrong, add what is missing.

Confirm the goal ranking, give one KPI number per goal, choose a Strategy Profile for the budget, confirm the budget split across goals, and name the anchor moments. Each Part ends with lettered YOUR INPUT boxes for exactly these.

Send the edited file to Paul Hinz (phinz@linuxfoundation.org). The 45-minute interview walks through your corrections; the Goals Summary and Budget Summary slides at the end become the first page of the final plan.

slides.name: The Story
slides.blurb: The era and its stakes, what makes x402 distinct from the alternatives, and the one-sentence positioning the plan hangs on. Drafted from the v3 Message Foundation and Brand Kit; market figures are web drafts to verify.

slides.title: The era: agents are becoming buyers, and the internet has no standard way to pay

era.head: Drafted era statement
era.text: The HTTP specification has carried 402 Payment Required since January 1997 (RFC 2068). For nearly three decades APIs, paywalls, and now AI agents have created accounts, passed forms, and managed keys before a cent moved. As agents become buyers, the industry needs a payment primitive built into the request-and-response cycle itself. x402 is that primitive, and in 2026 the largest payment networks, cloud providers, and stablecoin issuers chose to build it together under neutral governance at the Linux Foundation rather than each shipping their own.

slides.source: x402 Message Foundation v3 (S10, S24, elevator pitch); Juniper Research press release Apr 2026; McKinsey via secondary reports — market figures are drafts to verify.
slides.notes: Market figures found via web search 2026-09-30, not fetched in full; Morgan Stanley base case $190B US agentic commerce by 2030 is a third option. Ask the ED which one figure he trusts.

slides.title: The 'only place to…' positioning

dark.head: Drafted positioning sentence
dark.text: The x402 Foundation is the only place where the payment networks, cloud providers, stablecoin issuers, and commerce platforms that compete everywhere else sit at one table to set the open payment standard of the internet — and where no single one of them decides who may build on it.
dark.proof: Proof: 17 Premier members named July 14, 2026 · 54 member organizations in LFX (Sep 30, 2026) · charter §10 no exclusivity · every Participating Organization holds a TSC seat

cards.head: Locked positioning statement (v3)
cards.text: "…x402 is an open payment standard native to the internet. Any client pays any server in one request, on any supported network, with zero protocol fees and no accounts. Unlike account-first payment APIs, e-commerce rails built for human checkout, single-asset micropayment networks, and company-authored agent-payment standards, x402 is governed neutrally at the Linux Foundation and controlled by no single company."

slides.title: Project stage, what it implies, and what to retire

cards.head: Stage: has product and community
cards.text:
x402 has a shipping protocol (V2, Batch Settlement), 15 production facilitators and 1,400+ contributors, and a 54-organization membership. The Strategy deck's guidance for this stage: heavy focus on growth of members and on events/education.

What is different for x402: the community is large but mostly unattributed and unmeasured (no Lens keywords, no HubSpot property, no maintainer roster), and there are no owned events or courses yet. The first plan therefore buys measurement first, then seats.

cards.head: Implications for the goals
cards.text:
• Memberships lead (Goal 1): the Premier pipeline is warm (six intent signatories not yet members) and the first renewal cohort lands in Q2 2027.
• Audience building (Goal 2) needs a HubSpot property and Lens keywords before any number is credible — a Q4 2026 deliverable.
• Adoption (Goals 3–4) already has volume; the job is attribution and named proof.
• Fill the Seats (Goal 5) starts with presence at LF agentic events, not an owned conference.

cards.head: Proposed for retirement or re-scoping
cards.text:
• Any goal phrased around 'HTTP-native' as the differentiator — V2 is transport-agnostic and the ED de-emphasized HTTP in v3.
• 'Launch press release' as a Premier benefit — the operational launch has passed (MF YOUR INPUT 12).
• Cumulative 'over 100M payments' claim — retired from the Stat Bank.
• Rule of conflict: when two goals compete for budget, slot or spokesperson, the lower-numbered goal wins.

slides.source: LFX Marketing OS Strategy deck ('Focus May Vary Based on Project Type / Stage'); Message Foundation v3 change log.

slides.name: Budget
slides.blurb: The budget starts with one decision: your Strategy Profile. It sets the total as a percentage of membership revenue and pre-sets the paid-media share. The LF then splits the remainder across marketing services, third-party content and a discretionary reserve for hot and evergreen campaigns, and the total is allocated across the goals by the shares on the goal slides.

slides.title: Step 1 — Choose a Strategy Profile (the ED's decision)
slides.revenueLabel: = LFX list-price membership revenue as of Sep 30, 2026 (Premier $3.4M + General $675K). Confirm the dues-billed figure with finance.
slides.source: LF_Marketing_Services_Matrix (Strategy Profile, Flat Pricing tabs); LFX memberships by tier (2026-09-30). 60/20/20 split is a draft until LF confirms.
slides.notes: Strategy Profile: Conservative Growth 12% of revenue, paid 30% of total; Aggressive Scale 20%, paid 40%; Hyper-Growth 30%, paid 50%. Flat-pricing cross-check: LF Marketing Department tier (> $3M revenue) = $300K + 4% = $463,000, capped at $600K. The fee exceeds the 60% services bucket at all three profiles ($205K / $293K / $367K), so the interview must reconcile: move up a profile, reduce LF service scope, or change the split. Model computed by scripts/budget_model.py --revenue 4075000.

slides.title: Step 2 — How the budget is split, and what each bucket pays for

cards.head: Paid spend (pre-set by profile)
cards.text:

• Third-party developer newsletters and podcasts

PLANNED campaign spend.

cards.head: LF marketing services / headcount
cards.text:
Fractional or dedicated marketing lead, marcomms/PR, social, creative, web, marketing ops and reporting — the people who run the plan.

Draft: 60% of the remainder.

Cross-check against the flat-pricing fee for the Marketing Department tier ($463K). Where the fee exceeds the bucket, the ED and LF agree scope or move profile.

cards.head: Third-party content + Discretionary reserve
cards.text:
Third-party content (draft 20% of remainder): research reports, case studies, video, localization. PLANNED campaign spend.

Discretionary reserve (draft 20% of remainder): HOT campaigns — 72-hour response to news, releases, viral posts, competitor moves — and EVERGREEN activity (social, newsletter, inbound, SEO/AEO). Spent within limits, reported every QBR.

slides.source: LFX Marketing OS Strategy deck ('Budgets to Support Planned & Opportunistic Execution'); LF_Marketing_Services_Matrix pass-throughs.
